passage:
“Santosh, the last block!” Lalit said. Santosh set it on top of the tower and it stayed.
He looked at the tower, then at his father, then began to clap, fast, with a big open mouth.
“You did it! That's clapping for you!”
“Again,” Santosh said, and clapped again.
“Shall we clap together?”
Lalit clapped too, and they clapped in the same rhythm, badly, laughing.
Santosh flopped back on the mat, still clapping.

qa.q: What did Santosh place on top of the tower?
qa.a: The last block.

qa.q: What do Santosh's claps show he feels, and what else could they mean?
qa.a: They show pride and joy at the finished tower. He might also be copying the clapping his father does at his successes.

qa.q: What could Lalit do next?
qa.a: He could build another tower with Santosh and clap for tries as well as for finished towers.

qa.q: How might Lalit feel while clapping with him?
qa.a: He may feel happy and close to his son, because they share the moment.

grounding: A toddler claps at his own achievement and shares the joy with a parent who claps too.

passage: Toddler room note, Monday. Baljeet, almost two, clapped his hands the moment we began the morning song, first watching me, then laughing when the other children joined. Later, when Meher finished her puzzle, Baljeet clapped for her, even though he had not done it himself. He looked at me to see whether I was clapping too. I was. We ended up with a room full of clapping toddlers. 🙂 Lokesh

qa.q: What did Baljeet clap for after the morning song?
qa.a: He clapped for Meher when she finished her puzzle.

qa.q: What might Baljeet be feeling as he claps, and how can you tell?
qa.a: He seems happy and part of the group, shown by his laughing and his look to Lokesh to check that Lokesh was clapping too. He might partly be copying the others.

qa.q: How could Lokesh keep this happy routine going?
qa.a: Lokesh could make clapping a regular part of songs and successes so that children share joy together.

qa.q: What might Meher feel when Baljeet claps for her?
qa.a: She may feel proud and noticed, because a friend shared her success.

grounding: A toddler claps at a song and a friend's achievement, sharing joy and copying others in a happy social routine.

passage:
At the anganwadi in the village, Swati started the morning song, clapping on every beat. Minakshi sat in the front row. Her claps came late and messy, hands missing each other half the time, but she beamed at the children beside her.
When the song ended and everyone clapped fast, Minakshi clapped fastest of all, looking up at Swati to see if she'd noticed.

qa.q: Who started the morning song?
qa.a: Swati, clapping on every beat.

qa.q: Why did Minakshi look up at Swati after the song?
qa.a: She was delighted and proud of her fast clapping and wanted Swati to share her joy.

qa.q: What could Swati do when Minakshi looks up like that?
qa.a: She could smile and clap back at her, so Minakshi feels her joy is shared, without correcting her timing.

qa.q: How might the children beside Minakshi experience her beaming?
qa.a: They likely feel included in the fun, as clapping together makes the song a shared game.

grounding: A toddler claps along with a song, sharing joy and copying others even with messy timing.

passage:
On the floor of their Vancouver apartment, Wei had been trying to push the yellow star into the shape sorter for a long time. It finally dropped through with a clunk.
Wei looked at the hole, then at Layla, and clapped his hands, hard and happy.
Layla clapped too. "You did it!" Wei clapped again, then grabbed the next shape.

qa.q: Which shape did Wei finally push into the sorter?
qa.a: The yellow star.

qa.q: What did Wei's hard, happy clapping show?
qa.a: It showed delight and pride at getting the star in, and a wish to share it with Layla.

qa.q: What did Layla do that helped?
qa.a: She clapped with him and named his success, turning it into a happy shared moment.

qa.q: What would change if Layla had not looked up?
qa.a: Wei's joy would not have been shared, and he might not have felt so eager to try the next shape.

grounding: A toddler claps in delight at his own achievement and his mother claps with him.

passage: I'm Tarun, and my little brother Yogesh turned two last week. At his party, when Papa blew out the candles, Yogesh clapped and clapped. Later he climbed the step onto the sofa by himself and clapped again, looking at all of us. We all clapped back and he clapped harder. I don't think he knows what clapping is for. But he knows everyone smiles when he does it.

qa.q: How old did Yogesh turn?
qa.a: He turned two.

qa.q: What might Yogesh feel when he claps after climbing the step?
qa.a: He seems proud and delighted, and he wants everyone to share his joy, looking at them as he claps.

qa.q: What could the family keep doing when Yogesh claps?
qa.a: Clap back and smile, so clapping stays a happy thing they do together.

qa.q: How does Tarun see Yogesh's clapping?
qa.a: Tarun is amused and fond, thinking Yogesh doesn't understand clapping but knows it makes people smile.

grounding: A brother sees a toddler clap at candles and his own achievement, a happy shared routine.

passage:
Monday. Kavitha Aunty from next door sang a clapping song on the step. Ayesha watched her hands, completely still.
Wednesday. Kavitha sang it again. Ayesha brought her palms together, missed, tried again, and made a soft pat.
Saturday. Ayesha stacked three cups by herself, looked straight at Kavitha, and clapped, grinning. Kavitha clapped too. They clapped together until Ayesha fell over laughing.

qa.q: How many cups did Ayesha stack by herself on Saturday?
qa.a: She stacked three cups by herself.

qa.q: How can you tell Ayesha was proud on Saturday?
qa.a: She looked straight at Kavitha, grinned and clapped after stacking the cups, sharing her delight at her own achievement.

qa.q: How can an adult make clapping a happy routine?
qa.a: By singing clapping songs and clapping back with the child, as Kavitha did, so it becomes something they share.

qa.q: What is it like for Kavitha when Ayesha claps at her?
qa.a: Kavitha probably feels delighted and included, since Ayesha chose her to share the moment with.

grounding: It shows a toddler learning to clap at a song and then after an achievement, sharing joy and copying an adult.
